evidence.text: Q3 fuel very likely ran above Southwest's $3.70-3.75/gal guide assumption, which rested on the 17 July curve. Peers that reported after LUV last spoke came in over their own July assumptions by about $0.20: Alaska $3.94 against $3.75, United $3.90 against $3.69. On roughly 580m gallons a quarter (derived from the $889m Q2 y/y fuel increase), $0.20/gal is about $115m pre-tax, or about $0.17 of EPS before any fare recapture (UAL recaptured 72%). Net of recapture that is about $0.05-0.09 below the $0.625 guide midpoint, roughly onto the $0.57 consensus.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Q3 consensus is $0.57, below the $0.625 guide midpoint, after 16 down and 2 up revisions and a 3.4% drift down over 30 days. If the full fuel overrun were unpriced, consensus would still sit at or above the midpoint. What may remain is a residual of a few cents if Southwest's leisure-heavy domestic network recaptured less fuel through fares than UAL's.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide and the FY cut will be set at a much higher fuel price than anything Southwest has guided on. Peers' Q4 all-in assumptions are $4.65-4.85 (ALK, 20 Oct, which guides a Q4 loss of $2.00-2.50/share), about $4.80 (UAL, against Q3's $3.90) and about $4.25 (DAL on 9 Oct, before Brent reached $110 on 19 Oct). Southwest is unhedged after terminating its contracts. FY consensus of $2.88 already sits below the $3.25-4.25 guided floor, so the cut itself is expected. The open question is how far the Q4 guide falls below a consensus that is itself unsourced: about $0.9 is only implied by FY $2.88 less Q1 $0.45, Q2 $0.94 and Q3 $0.57. Each extra $0.50/gal on about 580m gallons is roughly $0.45/share.

What could be unpriced is the Q4 number: peers' consensus was stale by 40-50% on Q4 (UAL $1.00 midpoint against $1.88). If LUV's Q4 consensus has not caught up, the guide lands far below it. If the market had fully priced this, LUV would not have rallied 3.7% over 5 days into the print.

evidence.text: The sector's reaction function this week has been to buy fuel-driven guide-downs when demand holds. United guided Q4 EPS to $0.50-1.50 against about $1.88 consensus, said it is 'highly confident' of recapturing 100% of fuel with a lag, and saw sell-in yields up high-teens. Its shares rose about 4.8% after hours on 20 Oct (to $102.51 from $97.77) and were up again on 21 Oct. LUV rose about 2.7% intraday on 21 Oct in sympathy (24/7 Wall St widget, $39.55 to $40.74; baseline spot $40.78).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line cuts against LUV's own history: its last two guide cuts were sold (-6.19%, -4.07%). Among peers this month, DAL's cut was sold about 3% (9 Oct) and UAL's was bought about 5% (20-21 Oct). ALK's reaction to its 20 Oct loss guide was not found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: LUV has already rallied about 3.7% over 5 days, most of it on 21 Oct. The UAL template suggests investors are anchored on recapture with a lag rather than on Q4 EPS, so a Q4 guide far below a stale consensus may not be sold as hard as the July cut was. If this were fully in the price, the skew would have flattened from +3.7.
